persist

/per-SIST/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Persist means to continue firmly, especially in spite of difficulty or opposition.

The signal was faint and the storm was loud, but the radio operator persisted until someone finally answered.

Worked Example

The city denied Alma's community-garden permit in March. She revised the drainage plan and reapplied in May; denied again. She gathered four hundred signatures over the summer and presented them in September, where the council tabled the question twice. In January, a full year after her first application, the permit finally passed by one vote. Asked how she managed it, Alma shrugged: she had simply persisted while everyone else gave up.

Alma continues her campaign firmly through a full year of denials and delays, which is exactly what it means to persist in the face of opposition.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

endure: Endure means to last through hardship — to bear it without breaking. It is about withstanding, not advancing: you endure a storm; you persist in a campaign. Persist points the energy forward, firmly continuing an action against opposition, while endure holds position and takes the blows.

linger: Linger means to stay on longer than expected, passively and without effort — a guest lingers, a smell lingers, a doubt lingers. Persist is active and willful: firmly continuing in the face of difficulty. Things linger on their own; a person who persists is pushing on purpose.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

quit: to stop trying

surrender: to give up to opposition

Where it sits · how firmly one keeps going despite resistance — continue → persist → persevere

continue vs. persist: Continue is neutral and weaker — anything ongoing continues, with or without resistance; to persist is to keep going firmly against difficulty.

persevere vs. persist: Persevere is a shade stronger than persist: it emphasizes heroic steadiness through long hardship, while persist can also describe plain refusal to stop.

Which word fits?

Answer correctly to continue.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — per-

Prefix — per-: through, thoroughly

Root — sist

Root — sist: to stand (Latin sistere)

Put it together

Put it together: Persist comes from Latin persistere: per- (through) plus sistere (to stand). To persist is to stand your ground all the way through. The standing root sistere props up a whole English family — resist (stand against), insist (stand upon), consist (stand together) — and persist is the one that keeps standing when everything says sit down.

Use the root in a new word: resist

Use the root in a new word: resist: The old sea wall resisted wave after wave — resist means to stand against, from the same Latin sistere (to stand) that lets someone persist by standing firm through difficulty.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral; people, efforts, and stubborn things ('the cough persisted')

Persist is the verb; the related adjective persistent describes a person or thing that persists. The word is neutral about whether continuing is wise — admirable campaigns persist, but so do rumors and headaches.
